provenance.note: The catchment OUTLET, as a Point: the pick's {coordinates, name} verbatim, a (lon, lat) pair, 'lat,lon', a point layer, or a place name - the point the runoff drains to. It decides which basin is modelled at all, so it is asked for (picked on the canvas or passed explicitly) and NEVER invented [supplied on this invocation]
Constant design-storm intensity, used when no rain_window names a real event. A hypothetical storm, labeled as one [supplied on this invocation]
How long the design storm rains for [supplied on this invocation]
Total simulated window; longer than the rain to watch the recession [supplied on this invocation]

How wet the catchment already is: dry (SCS AMC I) | normal (AMC II) | wet (AMC III). The dominant infiltration lever - a wet basin absorbs far less and the hydrograph peaks higher and sooner [supplied on this invocation]
Result-writing cadence; a hydrograph resolved in six frames cannot be spot-checked against, so a short window wants a short interval [supplied on this invocation]
Solve sizing class [supplied on this invocation]

Apply the Huang (2006) steep-slope correction to the curve numbers using the mesh's own bed gradients. The engine's native branch is compiled off in the installed 9.0.0 build, so the correction is applied to the CN field before it is written [declared scenario default]
Land-cover product the per-node curve numbers and Manning n are keyed to [declared constant default]

Finest triangle edge, used where the mesh refines toward the channel network. THE granularity lever: peak depth and flooded extent are resolution-bound classes and a coarse mesh reads both low [declared scenario default]
Coarsest triangle edge, reached far from the channels on the hillslopes [declared scenario default]
Mesh gradation: how fast the edge length may grow between the channel band and the hillslopes [declared constant default]
Ground resolution the BARE-EARTH bed is sampled at the mesh nodes from; a surface model would put the bed on the forest canopy [declared constant default]
Channel network the mesh refinement is sized by distance to [declared constant default]
Solver time step. Overland sheet flow on a fine catchment mesh is CFL-tight, which is why it is seconds rather than tens of seconds [declared constant default]
not supplied; the run is named for its domain rather than for a place
not supplied; the analysis window is a +-0.14 deg buffer around the outlet
not supplied; the run is driven by the labeled constant design storm below
not supplied; curve numbers are distributed PER NODE from the land-cover raster
